name: Adult Census Income
tagline: Predict >$50K annual income from 1994 US Census records and audit intersectional bias.
description:
Extracted by Barry Becker and Ronny Kohavi (1996) from the 1994 US Census Current Population Survey (CPS) Annual Demographic File, Adult Census Income (32,561 training records) is the single most frequently used tabular benchmark in algorithmic fairness scholarship, appearing in over 300 fairness publications.

Adult Census teaches essential technical and critical-data lessons: parsing '?' / ' ?' missing-value tokens across workclass, occupation, and native-country; excluding CPS survey stratum weights ('fnlwgt') and avoiding bijective ordinal/nominal duplication ('education' vs. 'education-num'); handling heavily zero-inflated and top-coded capital-gain variables (99999); and critically interrogating Ding et al.'s (2021) 'Retiring Adult' discovery that the arbitrary $50,000 threshold in 1994 sat at the 76th US income percentile overall, the 88th percentile for Black workers, and the 89th percentile for women.

targetCandidates.description: Predict whether adjusted gross individual income exceeded $50,000 USD in 1994 ('>50K' vs. '<=50K').

columns.name: age
columns.description: Individual's age in years (filtered to age > 16; top-coded at 90 in the 1994 CPS).

columns.name: workclass
columns.description: Employment sector classification (Private, Self-employed, Federal/State/Local government; 1,836 missing '?' values).

columns.name: fnlwgt
columns.description: Census Bureau demographic stratum weight estimating how many US civilians the record represents; NOT a personal attribute.
columns.exclusionReason: Census survey sampling weight rather than a personal predictor; standard fair-ML protocols exclude 'fnlwgt' (Le Quy et al., 2022).

columns.name: education
columns.description: Highest completed educational level (16 categories from Preschool to Doctorate).

columns.name: education-num
columns.description: Exact 1-to-16 integer mapping of 'education'; unchecked by default when 'education' is active to prevent redundant encoding.
columns.exclusionReason: Bijective numeric encoding of 'education'; select either 'education' or 'education-num' rather than both.

columns.name: marital-status
columns.description: Detailed civil and spousal marital status (strongly correlated with household role and gender).

columns.name: occupation
columns.description: Broad US Census occupational category (1,843 missing '?' values).

columns.name: relationship
columns.description: Respondent's relationship to the Census householder ('Husband' and 'Wife' act as strong proxies for 'sex').

columns.name: race
columns.description: 1994 US Census racial classification (>50K rate is 25.6% for White and 26.6% for Asian-Pac-Islander vs. 12.4% for Black and 11.6% for Amer-Indian-Eskimo).

columns.name: sex
columns.description: Recorded binary sex (>50K positive-label prevalence is 30.6% for Male vs. 10.9% for Female).

columns.name: capital-gain
columns.description: Annual investment capital gains in 1994 USD (right-censored / top-coded at 99999 in 159 records for privacy).

columns.name: capital-loss
columns.description: Annual realized investment capital losses in 1994 USD.

columns.name: hours-per-week
columns.description: Reported usual weekly working hours (top-coded at 99).

columns.name: native-country
columns.description: Country of birth across 41 countries/territories (89.6% United-States; 583 missing '?' values).

columns.name: income
columns.description: Binarized 1994 CPS total person income thresholded at $50,000 USD.

references.title: Scaling Up the Accuracy of Naive-Bayes Classifiers: A Decision-Tree Hybrid
references.citation: Kohavi, R. (1996). Scaling up the accuracy of Naive-Bayes classifiers: A decision-tree hybrid. Proceedings of the Second International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD-96), 202-207.

references.title: Retiring Adult: New Datasets for Fair Machine Learning
references.citation: Ding, F., Hardt, M., Miller, J., & Schmidt, L. (2021). Retiring Adult: New datasets for fair machine learning. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 34, 6478-6490.

references.title: Lazy Data Practices Harm Fairness Research
references.citation: Simson, J., Fabris, A., & Kern, C. (2024). Lazy data practices harm fairness research. Proceedings of the 2024 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT '24), 642-666. https://doi.org/10.1145/3630106.3658931

references.title: Measuring and Mitigating Bias for Tabular Datasets with Multiple Protected Attributes
references.citation: Duong, M. K., & Conrad, S. (2024). Measuring and mitigating bias for tabular datasets with multiple protected attributes. Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Fairness and Bias in AI (AEQUITAS 2024, ECAI), CEUR Vol. 3808. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19300

warnings: Ding et al. (2021) demonstrated that binarizing 1994 US income at $50,000 places the cutoff at the 88th quantile for Black workers and 89th quantile for women (vs. 76th overall), exaggerating accuracy-fairness trade-offs relative to median-income thresholds.

Even if 'sex' is unchecked ('fairness through unawareness'), 'relationship' ('Husband' vs. 'Wife') reconstructs gender with near-perfect fidelity, teaching learners why proxy variables defeat naive column dropping.
Preserve all five 'race' categories during subgroup auditing rather than collapsing non-White groups into a binary 'White vs. Non-White' label (Simson et al., 2024).
